one_liner: A Senate staff role advising a senator or committee on health legislation and policy, likely drafting bills, briefing members, and meeting stakeholders.
fit_summary: The posting text is almost empty, but "Health Counsel" titles in Senate offices usually expect a law degree (JD) and substantial health policy experience. Daniel's strong policy knowledge and relationship skills are relevant, but nothing on file shows health-specific policy or legal background. Emergency-management consulting at IEM could connect only if Daniel worked on public health preparedness.
eligibility: The posting gives no eligibility details; open the full listing at the URL to confirm requirements before applying.
"Counsel" titles typically require a JD and bar membership. Verify this, because Daniel has no known law degree.
Senate offices are not covered by USAJOBS rules or the two-page OPM limit, and federal status is not required. Follow the office's own instructions instead.
Check whether the office is a personal office (which may prefer ties to the home state) or a committee (which may prefer a specific party affiliation).
strategy: Read the full posting on the Senate employment site first. The snippet here contains almost no detail, so confirm the requirements (especially a JD) before you invest time.
If you worked on public health emergency preparedness, pandemic response, or health-related disaster recovery at IEM, lead with that experience and describe it concretely.

Write a one-page, Hill-style resume plus a short cover letter that shows your command of policy, your stakeholder relationships, and your writing ability. Prepare a writing sample such as a policy memo.

If a JD is required, treat this as a networking target instead. Ask for informational conversations with health staffers and look for Legislative Assistant or Legislative Correspondent roles that cover health.
Apply quickly, because roles marked "open until filled" can close without notice.
resume_bullets: Advised [government client type] on [preparedness/recovery policy topic] at IEM, producing [number] briefings or memos for [audience].
Coordinated with [number/type] federal, state, and local stakeholders to [specific outcome you can verify].

Walk us through how you would brief the senator on a bill in 15 minutes.
How would you handle conflicting asks from stakeholders and constituent advocates?
Tell us about a policy document you wrote and how it was used.
